gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-noto-serif-hk: Horseshoe curves and sturdy diagonals give Cherry Swash a bold, single-thread swagger. Noto Serif HK follows with a generous gap at each curve's end and crossbars a touch thinner than the stems, so a long passage keeps moving smoothly.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-noto-serif-jp: Noto Serif JP draws a steady line with faint modulation, an unclenched c, and a literary hush beneath Cherry Swash. Its pencil-like partner never presses harder anywhere.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-noto-serif-kr: Cherry Swash bends its strokes like a paperclip, wide-mouthed and confident, with diagonals as heavy as the verticals. And Noto Serif KR takes over below with wide, barely curled s curves, so the body text can stay at a modest size.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-noto-serif-sc: Noto Serif SC rounds its letters gently and lets light through every c. Cherry Swash draws with one fixed nib, so its horseshoe curves stay bold while the body's slimmer horizontals add quiet literary refinement; a modest body size suits it.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-noto-serif-tc: Refined is the first impression of Noto Serif TC's held-open letters, yet Cherry Swash sits right above it with bowls that never thin at the sides. Noto Serif TC adds a quiet variation in line weight within each letter, which makes the heading's uniform strokes feel even more deliberate.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-petrona: Cherry Swash arrives with a horseshoe c and heavy diagonals. Petrona then softens the step from heavy to light strokes, with a shallow terminal curl and a wide gap, so a long passage neither jolts nor flattens.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-poly: Wire-thick strokes, horseshoe curves, real swagger: that's Cherry Swash. Poly is the bookish one, with mid-level contrast and terminals pulled back from each curve's close; the heading grabs attention while the body settles into reading.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-quattrocento: Quattrocento reads classic and traditional, with slimmer horizontals and daylight inside every curve, while Cherry Swash bends like neat pipe cleaner above it. And its diagonals, slightly lighter than the verticals, carry a longer passage along without any fuss.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-radley: Radley lets the eye slip in and out of its counters. Under Cherry Swash, with its shading-free strokes and horseshoe c, this classic serif carries a light touch of modulation that makes a long passage feel dignified and unhurried.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-roboto-serif: Roboto Serif reads classic and dignified, with big open eyes on every e and a and letters spaced well apart. But Cherry Swash does the loud work, with shadow-free strokes and a horseshoe c, while the body's worn-felt-marker swelling keeps things comfortable.
